newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dry weather returns to Western Europe.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dry weather returns to Western Europe.

text.p: Dry weather has returned to the parched farming areas of western Europe, but there are signs of more rain from the weekend, forecasters said.

Cereal farmers and the water industry are still desperate for rain, despite wet weather at the start of this week. The rain was not enough to enable crops to recover from the effects of a prolonged dry spell.
Dry and warm weather was back in France on Wednesday with only scattered showers lingering over eastern regions, forecasters said.
"The high pressure system is coming back from the west but there are still a few showers in the east," Meteo France said.
For Thursday, sunshine was expected to make a comeback across France apart from a few showers on the Mediterranean island of Corsica and in the mountainous southeast.
The warm and dry weather was expected to persist through Saturday, forecasters said.
Dry weather has also returned to the eastern grain producing areas of Britain, but colder, more unsettled weather is likely to bring rain from Saturday.

North-east Norfolk had just 1.5 millimetres of rainfall late Tuesday, a spokesman for the London Weather Centre said, but in the counties to the south -- Essex and Suffolk -- there was not enough rain to wet the ground.
A cold front is due to cross the country on Saturday, a spokesman for the Meteorological Office said. "It looks like it will be unsettled over the weekend," he said, with rain possible.
Rain in the past few days has pushed down cereals prices in Britain, Spain, Portugal and parts of France, after a series of rises triggered by fears over the effects of the long dry spell.
Western Europe is trending cooler with a chance of scattered showers in the north and with the rest of the region drier and much cooler, private forecaster Weather Services Corp said.
The UK has a chance of a few showers that will favour the north. Temperatures will be below normal.
Germany and Central Europe will be much cooler with a chance of showers early in the period. Temperatures will be below to well below normal.
Southern Europe will be seasonably warm with an increasing chance of scattered showers late in the period.

"The 1990s have seen extremes of both flood and drought in Britain, but the question of whether this period is a reflection of a permanent change in the country's climate remains tantalisingly unclear," according to UK Meteorological Office Water Services Manager Mary Clarke.

Writing in the Office's Outlook publication she said there was considerable pressure on resources on a regional scale, even though the UK as a whole is well supplied with water. "With a long term climate change, the impact on the water industry could be severe," Clarke said.
